description: This practical course develops hands-on understanding of control system characteristics, time-domain and frequency-domain analysis, error detectors, conventional controllers, motor control, compensator design and industrial process control.
experiments: Obtain the step response of first-order and second-order systems and determine the time-domain specifications from their transfer functions.
Determine the characteristics of LVDT and potentiometer error detectors for control applications.
Obtain the response of P, PI, PD, PID and relay control actions on one-time-constant and two-time-constant processes with and without delay.

Study a thermal system and its temperature control by finding its transfer function from the open-loop time response, determining the closed-loop response using PID and relay control actions, and comparing the results.
Study the performance of DC motor position control.
Obtain the speed-torque characteristics of an AC servomotor and determine the speed-control characteristics of a DC motor with a control parameter.
Design a lag or lead compensator for a given system, obtain its frequency response and analyze the result.
For a given transfer-function or state-space system, perform simulations in MATLAB to obtain time-domain specifications, frequency-domain specifications and stability.
Study the performance of an industrial process for level control and flow control.
